title: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Yose
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was a student of Rabbi Oshaya, as in Sanhedrin 112a: “Rabbi Chama bar Yose said that Rabbi Oshaya said”; there, 16b, it reads Rabbi Chiyya bar Yosef. In Avodah Zarah 44b: “Rabbi Chama bar Yosef Berabbi said that Rabbi Oshaya said” (Hyman proposes “Rabbi Chama bar Yosef said that Rabbi Oshaya Berabbi said,” according to Dikdukei Soferim): “Rabban Gamliel gave a stolen answer,” etc., “and I say it is not stolen.” In Niddah 19a he spoke in Rabbi Oshaya’s name: “What is the verse?” etc.

In Rabbi Yochanan’s days he was already the elder of the generation, and he was then the head in Chamat Gader (near Tiberias, as in Eruvin 5:7), as in Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 6:4: Rabbi Chiyya (bar Abba), Rabbi Yasa and Rabbi Imi went up to Chamat Gader and asked Rabbi Chama bar Yosef, who permitted it; Rabbi Yochanan heard and said, “You did well.” In the Babylonian Talmud, Eruvin 65b, the statement is cited: “Rabbi Chanina (Hyman proposes Rabbi Chama, according to Rabbeinu Chananel and Dikdukei Soferim) bar Yosef, Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba and Rabbi Assi came to a certain inn … Rabbi Chama bar Yosef said, ‘Let us rent’; Rabbi Ami [said], ‘Let us not rent.’ Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to them, ‘Let us rely on the words of an elder’ (Rabbi Chama bar Yosef). They came and asked Rabbi Yochanan, who said to them, ‘You did well to rent.’” In Orlah 2:5 Rabbi Chama bar Yosef raised an objection before Rabbi Yochanan. He is likewise mentioned in Avodah Zarah 14b: “When Rav Dimi came, he said that Rabbi Chama bar Yosef said: Kuriyati.”

notes.text: The heading’s Yose and the body’s Yosef are retained. Berabbi shifts from Chama to Oshaya only in Hyman’s proposed reading, kept distinct from his quoted text. קורייטי remains Kuriyati. Hyman’s identification of the elder in the parallel Eruvin narratives is preserved as his argument.

The consulted Avodah Zarah 44b places Berabbi with Chama bar Yosef before the Oshaya transmission. Hyman proposes moving the designation to Oshaya. The Yose/Yosef and Assi/Ami forms and his identification of the elder across the two Eruvin narratives remain separately qualified.
